record.original_question: Given two non-cospectral graphs of the same order that appear, from numerical computation, to have equal graph energy, find a general proof method that can rigorously establish that they are equienergetic. Here the energy of a graph is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and two graphs of the same order are equienergetic when these energies are equal.

evidence.quote: (2) If by numerical calculation one finds that two non-cospectral graphs seem to be equienergetic, in the general case no method is known for proving that this indeed is the case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix A(G), and let λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n denote the (real) eigenvalues of A(G). Define the energy of G by

  E(G) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|.

Two graphs G and H of the same order n are called cospectral if A(G) and A(H) have the same multiset of eigenvalues, and equienergetic if E(G) = E(H). Note that cospectral graphs are automatically equienergetic, so the interesting case is non-cospectral equienergetic pairs.

Problem. Develop a general proof method with the following property: given any two non-cospectral graphs G and H of the same order n whose energies, computed numerically, appear to coincide, the method rigorously establishes (or refutes) the exact equality E(G) = E(H). Equivalently, find a general technique that, applied to an arbitrary pair of non-cospectral graphs of the same order, decides whether they are equienergetic without relying on a specific ad hoc construction.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as an open problem in spectral graph theory. While many ad hoc constructions of non-cospectral equienergetic graph pairs and infinite families exist (via graph operations, line graphs, signed graphs, complementary equienergetic graphs, etc.), recent literature continues to state that no general method is known to prove equienergeticity of two arbitrary non-cospectral graphs whose energies merely appear numerically equal.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems for Equienergetic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: If by numerical calculation one finds that two non-cospectral graphs seem to be equienergetic, in the general case no method is known for proving that this indeed is the case.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A graph operation and its applications in generating orderenergetic and equienergetic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Corresponding to any given graph, we can generate an infinite sequence of pair of equienergetic non-cospectral graphs using this graph operation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works only provide ad hoc construction methods, not a general proof method.

status_evidence.title: On the construction of L-equienergetic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: In general the problem of constructing L-equienergetic graphs from any pair of given graphs is still not solved.
status_evidence.claim: Related general construction/proof problems remain unsolved.
